statement: For every fixed \(0<a\le1\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), uniformly for real \(T\ge3\) and \(3/5\le\sigma<1\), the multiplicity count of nontrivial zeta zeros satisfying \(\Re\rho>\sigma\) and \(T\le\Im\rho\le T+T^a\) is \(O_{a,\varepsilon}(T^{(1-\sigma)\max\{15a/(3+5\sigma),\,2\max(a,2/3)\}+\varepsilon})\). At \(a=3/5,\sigma=3/4\) this is \(O_\varepsilon(T^{1/3+\varepsilon})\); enlarging directly to the \(a=2/3\) estimate of Ye Theorem 1.2 gives \(O_\varepsilon(T^{10/27+\varepsilon})\).
dependencies: Uniformity in the real start of the Heath-Brown–Iwaniec short-interval fourth moment as quoted by Ye
derivation: For \(0<a<2/3\) and each real \(U\ge3\), positivity gives \(\int_U^{U+U^a}|\zeta(1/2+it)|^4dt\le \int_U^{U+U^{2/3}}|\zeta(1/2+it)|^4dt\ll_\eta U^{2/3+\eta}\) for every \(\eta>0\). This extension holds for every start \(U\), including the \(O(1)\) starts used to cover the enlarged Type II integral. For \(a\ge2/3\), use (2.17) with the same \(a\). Apply Theorem 1.1 with \(\ell=2\) and \(\theta=\max(a,2/3)\), so the denominator is exactly \(2\). No zero-free half-plane input.

statement: Assume as a separate external input that every nontrivial zero of \(\zeta(s)\) has real part at most \(7/8\). Fix a real \(\alpha\ne0\) and a smooth function \(\phi\in C_c^\infty((-1,1))\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\), uniformly for all sufficiently large real \(K\), the smoothed oscillatory prime-power sum \(\sum_{n\ge1}\Lambda(n)e^{2\pi i\alpha n^{3/5}}\phi((n-K)/K^{7/10})\) is \(O_{\alpha,\phi,\varepsilon}(K^{27/40+\varepsilon})\). This is \(m=1\), \(\beta=3/5\), \(\delta=7/10\) in Ye (1.7)–(1.9). The estimate is pointwise in the window center \(K\), with no averaging over \(K,\alpha\), or \(\phi\), and with the nonzero phase fixed. Its exponent improves \(44/65+\varepsilon\) from direct substitution in Ye Theorem 1.3 at those same parameters and cutoff. It makes no claim for the unphased prime count or the global prime number theorem.
dependencies: External fixed zero-free cutoff \(\Reho\le7/8\) as in Ye §4
derivation: \(b=3/5\), \(v=w_0=q=a_0=3/10\). Proposition 3.3 gives a zero window \(J\) at absolute height \(\asymp K^{3/5}\) of length \(O(K^{3/10+\eta})\) and the factor \(K^{-3/10}\), with arbitrary power error. The sign of the window can be reflected for zeta. For fixed sufficiently small \(0<\eta<1/100\), cover \(J\) by \(O(1)\) windows at starts \(T\asymp K^{3/5}\) with \(a=(3/10+2\eta)/(3/5)\in(1/2,2/3)\). Here \(15a/(3+5\sigma)\le (5/2)a<4/3\) after choosing \(\eta\) sufficiently small. The new local count is \(O(K^{(4/5)(1-\sigma)+\varepsilon})\) uniformly for \(3/5\le\sigma<1\). Zeros with \(1/2\le\Re\rho\le3/5\) contribute \(O(K^{9/10+\eta+\varepsilon})\) to the weighted sum \(\sum_{\rho:\gamma\in J,\Re\rho\ge1/2}K^{\Re\rho}\), by subdividing into unit height intervals. For \(\Re\rho>3/5\), partial summation uses the local density count, with its lower-boundary term and inclusive \(7/8\) endpoint. The affine exponent \(\sigma+(4/5)(1-\sigma)\) has maximum \(39/40\) at \(7/8\). Multiplying by \(K^{-3/10}\) yields \(27/40\). The formula in Ye's preprint uses \(\nu=\max(q,2b/3)=2/5\), so \(Q(2/5)-3/10=7/10+18/65-3/10=44/65\); the difference is \(1/520\).

statement: Fix \(0<d<2/5\) and fixed constants \(c,C>0\). For \(T\to\infty\), uniformly over real \(U\in[cT,CT]\), the sum of \(e^{2y}/(1+y^2)\) over zeta zero copies with \(U\le\Im\rho\le U+U^{3/5}\), \(1/2\le\Re\rho\le1-d\), and \(y=(\Re\rho-1/2)\log T\), is \(O_{d,\varepsilon,c,C}(T^{1-d/2+\varepsilon})\) for each \(\varepsilon>0\), hence \(o(T)\). This is a single-height-window estimate and does not imply global weighted BGSTB tightness.
derivation: Below \(3/5\), the local total count and the trivial exponential weight bound give \(O(T^{4/5+\varepsilon})\). Above \(3/5\), the local count has slope at most \(3/2\); counting bins of width \(1/\log T\) and multiplying by the exponential weight gives exponent \(1-(1-\sigma)/2+\varepsilon\le1-d/2+\varepsilon\). Adjust a strict counting threshold by \(1/\log T\) at grid boundaries, using the trivial bound on the resulting overlap around \(3/5\). Covering \([T,2T]\) would cost \(O(T^{2/5})\) windows. This removes the saving. No fixed zero-free cutoff is needed for the stated real-part slice.
